newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Judge in Hong Kong fraud case asks to retire early.
newsitem.headline: Judge in Hong Kong fraud case asks to retire early.

text.p: A Hong Kong judge in the centre of a scandal over allegations New Zealand officials tried to interfere in a fraud case has sought early retirement on medical grounds, the government said.

Judge Brian Caird, a New Zealander, was alleged in August to have complained to senior Hong Kong government lawyers that two fellow judges had tried to influence him in a fraud case against New Zealander Aaron Nattrass.

Immigration consultant Nattrass, 34, has denied 35 fraud charges, including obtaining more than HK$500,000 (NZ$94,750) through making false promises to Hong Kong residents of employment and residency in New Zealand.
Caird was said to have complained that the New Zealand Immigration Service appeared to be using the two judges to influence him and that the New Zealand Consulate had said Nattrass was guilty.
The allegations were later denied by New Zealand Foreign Affairs Minister Don McKinnon as "wrong".
Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten was considering Caird's early retirement request, the government statement said on Friday night.
The request, which comes 10 months before his official retirement, would be considered by an independent medical board.

The South China Morning Post, citing a statement released by Caird's lawyer, reported that the judge had explained he "may have been suffering from an acute confused state and was delusional" and brain tests indicated he had an "abnormality of the right parietal lobe of the brain".
Neither Caird nor his lawyer Jonathan Midgley was immediately available for comment.
